svg.aria-label: The Google Calendar database schema. Calendars belong to a user and hold events. An event row carries its calendar, its start and end time in UTC, whether it recurs, and a foreign key to its recurrence rule. Event_recurrence_rules holds one rule per recurring series, giving frequency, interval and end date, so occurrences are computed rather than stored. Event_exceptions holds one row per occurrence that was cancelled or replaced. Invitations hold one row per invited user per event with an RSVP status.
svg.text: One rule per series, not one row per date.
One row only when an occurrence differs.
Why a recurring event is not a row per occurrence
A meeting every Monday with no end date would be an unbounded number of rows.
The series is one event plus one rule, and the dates are worked out when a week is read.
Cancel or move a single occurrence and that one date gets an exception row, nothing else.
